The complete description of the reasoning is below:<</think> <answer>\[S = \sum_{k=1}^{2007}\sqrt{1+\dfrac1{k^2}+\dfrac1{(k+1)^2}}\]can be simplified by recognizing that: \[\sqrt{1+\dfrac1{k^2}+\dfrac1{(k+1)^2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{k^2(k+1)^2 + k^2 + (k+1)^2}{k^2(k+1)^2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{(k^2+k+1)^2+1}{k^2(k+1)^2}}\]This can be further simplified to: \[\sqrt{\dfrac{(k^2+k+1)^2+1}{k^2(k+1)^2}} = \dfrac{k^2+k+1}{k(k+1)} = \dfrac{k^2+k}{k(k+1)} + \dfrac{1}{k(k+1)} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{k} - \dfrac{1}{k+1} \]Since the difference of \(1/k\) and \(1/(k+1)\) disappears when telescoping, \[S = 1 + \dfrac{1}{1} - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{2007} - \dfrac{1}{2008} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{1} - \dfrac{1}{2008} = 2 - \dfrac{1}{2008} = \dfrac{4015}{2008}\]The square of \(S\) is \[S^2 = \left(\dfrac{4015}{2008}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4015^2}{2008^2} = \dfrac{16120225}{4032064}\] Since \(16120225/4032064 \approx 3.9897\) and \(\lfloor 3.9897 \rfloor = 3\), the answer is \(\boxed{3}\)</answer>
